# T3 Code patch ledger

Every vendored file Rennet has changed from the pristine snapshot on the `t3-vendor` branch, with why. `pnpm t3:check-ledger` fails on any vendored file that differs from the snapshot and is not listed here. Paths are relative to `vendor/t3code/`. Rennet-owned files inside the tree (`UPSTREAM.json`, this file, `digests/`, any `project.json`, any `tsconfig.rennet.json`) never need a row.

Prefer extension over edit: put Rennet code outside `vendor/` and import their modules. When upstream merges a change listed here, the fold that brings it in removes the row.

| File | Reason | Upstreamable | Upstream PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts` | Checkpoints carry optional `startCommandId` for exact round-attempt recovery. `thread.turn.start` (both command shapes) and the `thread.turn-start-requested` payload carry an optional `outputSchema`, so a turn can declare a structured-output contract. Rennet's board seats need one JSON board per turn. The same three shapes also carry an optional `mcpServers` (`name → { url, bearerTokenEnvVar? }`), so a caller can hand a turn its own MCP servers. The field names the environment variable holding the credential and never the credential: this command is persisted to the event store and replayed from it, and the Claude SDK puts its whole MCP option on the child's argument list. Server names are constrained to a TOML bare key because Codex writes them into a dotted config path, where a dot silently makes a nested table. `thread.create` (both command shapes) and the `thread.created` payload carry an optional `instructions` (a system-prompt append) and the same optional `mcpServers`, and the `OrchestrationThread` projection carries both: every turn on a Rennet session thread — including the ones the user starts from the composer, which Rennet does not author — has to run under the review's briefing and with Rennet's tools, and a provider session is built on the thread's FIRST turn, so this is a thread fact and not a turn one. The `TurnMcpServer*` schemas moved above `OrchestrationThread` because a `Schema.Struct` evaluates its field schemas at module load and the thread projection now references them. The guarantee is the dedicated credential field only — `url` is any trimmed string, so a token in a query parameter still reaches the store and the argument list. The file also defines `TurnMcpServer`/`TurnMcpServers`, the name the server owns (`SIDECAR_OWNED_MCP_SERVER_NAME`), and the helpers every hop shares (`normalizeTurnMcpServers`, `differingTurnMcpServerNames`, `collidingTurnMcpServerNames`). | yes | pending |
| `packages/contracts/src/provider.ts` | `ProviderSessionStartInput` and `ProviderSendTurnInput` carry `outputSchema` and `mcpServers`. `ProviderService` re-decodes both and strips unknown keys, so a field has to exist on the schema to survive the hop. Both also carry the THREAD's `instructions`: a provider fixes its system prompt when the session process is created, so the briefing is a session-level fact, and it travels on the turn as well so a session recovered for that turn starts briefed rather than bare. | yes | pending |
| `packages/contracts/src/providerRuntime.ts` | Optional `TurnCompletedPayload.usageEpoch` identifies the Claude runtime counter (#775). `ThreadTokenUsageSnapshot` also carries Codex cumulative counters and provider thread identity separately from context usage (#776). `TurnCompletedPayload` carries `structuredOutput` and `durationMs`, the two facts the SDK result frame already reports and T3 dropped. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/orchestration/decider.ts` | Copies the command's `outputSchema` and `mcpServers` onto the `thread.turn-start-requested` event it emits. Copies `thread.create`'s `instructions` and `mcpServers` onto the `thread.created` event, so the thread record carries the briefing for its whole life. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.ts` | Persists the accepted start command to exact provider turn association, hidden from the chat timeline. Threads `outputSchema` and `mcpServers` from the turn-start event into both `ProviderSessionStartInput` (the session starts on the first turn) and `ProviderSendTurnInput`. Reads the THREAD's `instructions` and `mcpServers` off the read model and puts them on `ProviderSessionStartInput`, and on every `ProviderSendTurnInput` so a recovery has them. The session's MCP set is the UNION of the thread's and the turn's, computed once in `unionThreadAndTurnMcpServers` and used for both, because the adapter fixes that union when the session process is created and compares every later turn against it. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts` | Stamps settlements with a usage epoch combining query identity and SDK session identity, covering recovered queries and in-query `/clear` resets (#775). Sets the SDK's `outputFormat: { type: "json_schema", schema }` from the session's `outputSchema`, remembers the contract on the session context, fails a later turn whose schema the live session cannot serve (the SDK fixes `outputFormat` at `query()` construction and offers no setter) and says which of the two ways it failed, and puts `structured_output`/`duration_ms` from the result frame on `turn.completed`. Merges the turn's caller-supplied `mcpServers` into the SDK's and refuses a caller server under a name T3's own server holds, rather than dropping it — dropping left the session storing one set and comparing another, so the turn that opened the session was rejected as a mismatch against itself. EVERY credential is a `${VAR}` reference, T3's own included: its bearer goes into the child environment as `T3_MCP_BEARER_TOKEN`, because the SDK serialises this whole option into one `--mcp-config <json>` argument. Remembers the set on the session context and refuses a later turn asking for a different set by the names it disagrees on — the SDK fixes `mcpServers` at `query()` construction exactly as it fixes `outputFormat`, and `strictMcpConfig` is deliberately not set. Also spawns the Claude child through the SDK's `spawnClaudeCodeProcess` hook so its stdin has an `error` listener: the SDK's own transport writes the prompt without one, and a `claude` that dies before that write raised an unhandled `write EPIPE` that killed the whole server process. Binds SDK control requests to the owning child exit/error or explicit query close, so dead transports cannot leave them pending. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.ts` | `sendTurn` carries the turn's `outputSchema` and `mcpServers` into the session `resolveRoutableSession`/`recoverSessionForThread` recovers from a persisted resume cursor. Claude's SDK fixes `outputFormat` when the query is built, so a session recovered without it could never serve the turn that asked for the recovery: the adapter refused the turn as a schema mismatch, against a contract identical to the thread's own. The same recovery path carries the thread's `instructions`: a session recovered without it runs every turn after a daemon restart unbriefed, silently. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.test.ts` | Covers the recovery above: a stale `claudeAgent` session recovered for a turn starts on that turn's output schema, and on that turn's MCP servers. The MCP case is the only test that crosses `ProviderSendTurnInput`, which is re-decoded here and strips any key it does not declare. Also covers the thread's briefing: a stale `claudeAgent` session recovered for a briefed thread starts on the briefing and the thread's servers. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexAdapter.ts` | Preserves Codex cumulative usage breakdowns with the notification's exact turn id, including reported zero (#776). Forwards a turn's `outputSchema` to the Codex session runtime, and lowers caller-supplied `mcpServers` to `-c mcp_servers.<name>.url=…` plus `-c mcp_servers.<name>.bearer_token_env_var="…"`, naming the variable the daemon set and never carrying a credential. The credential key is written only when the caller declared one: an empty override makes Codex expect a bearer it cannot resolve, which against a real MCP server is zero requests where omitting it handshakes. Codex deep-merges every `-c` into the user's own config at every depth with no way to remove a key, so a same-named server would trade credentials and headers; the adapter therefore reads the user's configured server names (`codexConfiguredMcpServerNames`) and REFUSES a colliding caller name, the sidecar's own name included, rather than trying to out-merge it. Nothing is filtered out of the caller's set, so the session stores and compares the same thing. The adapter also states `sidecarMcpServerConfigured` rather than letting a name imply it. Codex reads its MCP configuration when the app-server is spawned, so a later turn asking for a different set is refused the way Claude's is. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexSessionRuntime.ts` | `buildTurnStartParams` passes `outputSchema` through to `V2TurnStartParams.outputSchema`, which the generated protocol already carries and T3 was dropping. Splits the MCP question in two: `hasConfiguredMcpServer` still answers the tool-catalog reload for any inline server, while `browserToolsAvailable` reads the new `sidecarMcpServerConfigured` option, which the adapter states. A name cannot answer it — a caller supplying a server called `t3-code` would satisfy any name test — and describing browser tools the session does not have is a lie in the Codex prompt. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts` | Preserves Claude usage epochs and cumulative `modelUsage` on durable settlements (#775). Persists a Codex counter baseline at turn start and carries it plus the final counter into settlement, surviving the bounded activity window and restart (#776). Projects a `turn.settled` activity from `turn.completed`, carrying the settled turn's structured output, duration, usage and cost. Nothing else in the projection carried a turn's own result, so a reader over `orchestration.subscribeThread` could not see it. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.test.ts` | Covers the new adapter behaviours above: the schema becomes the SDK's `outputFormat`, no schema means no output format, a turn asking for a different contract than its session is refused, a turn arriving on a session that holds no contract is refused as that rather than as a mismatch, and the spawn hook terminates a child whose stdin breaks instead of letting the EPIPE escape. Also covers the caller-supplied MCP servers: both credentials travel as `${VAR}` references, a caller name colliding with T3's own is refused, the turn that opened the session is accepted rather than rejected against itself, no servers means no `mcpServers` option at all, and a turn asking for a different set — including one differing only in its credential variable — is refused with the differing names and the wording that says settings differ. One case drives the REAL SDK through the spawn hook WITH a live sidecar session and reads the argument vector it built, asserting neither the caller's nor the sidecar's credential is on it; the `--mcp-config` serialisation is downstream of this adapter and cannot be seen by reading it. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexAdapter.test.ts` | Covers the Codex leg of the caller-supplied MCP servers: the arguments name the credential variable and carry no credential, a server declaring none gets no credential key at all, a name the sidecar or the user's own config holds is refused while a free name starts normally, the turn that opened the session is accepted, a caller-named `t3-code` claims no provenance, and a turn asking for a different set is refused. Also unit-tests the config name scanner against the four forms a server is declared in. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexSessionRuntime.test.ts` | Covers what the reload predicate answers, and states plainly that it is name-blind by design — the browser question is settled by provenance in the integration test, not here. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexCollabRuntime.integration.test.ts` | Drives the real session runtime against the scripted app-server for the two behaviours the predicate split exists for, neither of which can be reached by calling a predicate: the tool-catalog reload happens BEFORE `turn/start`, and the turn's own developer instructions describe browser tools only when the sidecar's server is attached — including the case where a caller took the `t3-code` name. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/provider/testFixtures/codexCollabMockPeer.mjs` | An opt-in `recordAllRequests` that appends every request the runtime sends, in order, to its own sidecar file. The existing `recordRequests` records `thread/resume` only and its file is compared exactly, so ordering assertions needed a separate record rather than a widened one. | yes | pending |
| `packages/contracts/src/orchestration.test.ts` | Covers the turn's MCP servers at the contract: an endpoint and a credential variable NAME decode, a raw credential has nowhere to live, a server name Codex could not write into its config path is refused, and so is a credential variable that is not an environment variable name. Covers the same for a THREAD's briefing and servers: `thread.create` decodes with and without both fields, a raw credential still has nowhere to live, and the `thread.created` payload and the thread projection carry them. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/orchestration/projector.ts` | Projects `thread.created`'s `instructions` and `mcpServers` onto the in-memory thread the same way the SQL projection does. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionPipeline.ts` | Persists the thread's `instructions` and `mcpServers` on the `thread.created` upsert. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/persistence/Services/ProjectionThreads.ts` | The projected thread row carries the thread's `instructions` and `mcpServers`. Both are optional so a row read by a query that does not select the two columns still decodes. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/ProjectionThreads.ts` | The `projection_threads` upsert and reads carry `instructions` and `mcp_servers_json` (the servers as JSON text, like `model_selection_json`). | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/persistence/Migrations.ts` | Adds the two `projection_threads` columns after the migrator instead of as a migration, because the migrator runs only ids GREATER than the highest id recorded and silently skips the rest: a fork that takes id 45 makes upstream's own 45 unrunnable on every database that ran ours, and a fork that takes 900 makes every future upstream migration unrunnable. Neither fails loudly. The statements are `PRAGMA`-guarded and idempotent, so upstream's id space stays untouched and a fold never has to renumber anything. | no | n/a |
| `apps/server/src/ws.ts` | Forwards the bootstrap `createThread` shape's `instructions` and `mcpServers` into the `thread.create` it dispatches, so the field the contract accepts is not silently dropped one hop later. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.test.ts` | Covers the thread-level briefing end to end through the real engine and projection: a thread created with `instructions` and a server starts its session on both, the turn carries both so a recovery has them, the session's set is the union of the thread's and the turn's, and the thread read back out of the projection still carries the pair. | yes | pending |
| `apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts` | Projects exact start command identity onto checkpoints from the durable provider start association, independent of bounded activity history. The shell queries do not: `OrchestrationThreadShell` carries neither. | yes | pending |
